newsitem.title: ITALY: New 18-mo CTZs could help Italy's 1997 PSBR - BCI.
newsitem.headline: New 18-mo CTZs could help Italy's 1997 PSBR - BCI.

text.p: Italy's 1997 public sector borrrowing requirement (PSBR) could benefit from the issue of new 18-month zero coupon Treasury certificates (CTZ) to be introduced next month, Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) said.
BCI research unit noted in a report that the level of PSBR was directly linked to the type of debt instrument chosen to cover the deficit.
The Treasury said last week it would issue a new CTZ with a duration of 18 months in mid-January.
It said the new issue would be alongside the traditional 24-month CTZs and its auction timetable would coincide with short-term bills (BOTS) and two-year CTZs.
The government has set a 1997 PSBR target of 61.4 trillion lire which takes into account the just approved austerity budget which aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire from next year's projected deficit.
BCI noted that the margin between issue and redemption price for BOTs went down in the state accounts as interest charges at the moment of issue and not on maturity as is the case for CTZs.
In 1996, the report said, CTZ spreads accounted for over 8.5 trillion lire, a sum not included in this year's PSBR calculations.
But BCI said the new 18-month CTZ could produce savings for the state accounts.
As an example, it said that if the amount of three-month BOTs issued at auction twice a month was reduced by 1.5 trillion lire, this amount could be counterbalanced by the issue of 18-month CTZs.
Total savings in 1997 could therefore be some 4.40 trillion lire, according to BCI calculations.
The first 18-month CTZs to be issued will mature in July 1998, BCI noted, when it was likely to be clear which European Union members would join the single currency right from the start.

"In other words, the Italian government will still have the first half of 1988 in which to benefit from the accounting bonus deriving from the new CTZs," the BCI report said. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
